title: Low-intensity pulsed ultrasound activates Piezo1 to restore brain lymphatic drainage and improve outcomes in traumatic brain injury mice
title_zh: 低强度脉冲超声激活Piezo1，恢复脑淋巴引流并改善创伤性脑损伤小鼠的预后
abstract: BACKGROUND: Meningeal lymphatic vessels (mLVs) are specialized lymphatic structures that drain cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) and facilitate immune surveillance of the central nervous system. This drainage system is impaired after traumatic brain injury (TBI); mLVs undergo structural regression, and CSF outflow to peripheral lymphoid tissues is markedly slowed. The resulting accumulation of hyperphosphorylated tau, amyloid-β, and inflammatory mediators drives sustained neuroinflammation and cognitive decline. The neuroprotective effect of low-intensity pulsed ultrasound (LIPUS) in TBI mice has been previously demonstrated, however, its impact on brain lymphatic drainage is unclear. METHODS: Here, we employed a controlled cortical impact (CCI) mouse model of TBI combined with serial LIPUS stimulation to investigate its therapeutic potential for mLV function. RESULTS: LIPUS restored neurological function in TBI mice, improving motor coordination and spatial/recognition memory while attenuating tau pathology, Aβ burden, and astrocyte reactivity. Mechanistically, LIPUS activated Piezo1 on meningeal lymphatic endothelial cells (LECs), triggering a downstream signaling cascade that promoted LEC proliferation and migration in vitro and restored lymphatic coverage and drainage function in vivo. To identify the critical mediator of this process, we examined the pathway's downstream components and found that vascular endothelial growth factor C (VEGFC) served as the critical downstream effector: VEGFC overexpression rescued meningeal lymphatic restoration and CSF drainage. CONCLUSIONS: These results establish LIPUS as a non-invasive therapeutic strategy that functionally restores brain lymphatic drainage after TBI, representing a promising preclinical therapeutic strategy for proteinopathy-associated neurological diseases that warrants further optimization for clinical translation.
abstract_zh: 背景：脑膜淋巴管（mLVs）是专门的淋巴结构，负责引流脑脊液（CSF）并促进中枢神经系统的免疫监视。创伤性脑损伤（TBI）后，该引流系统受损；mLVs 发生结构退化，CSF 向外周淋巴组织的流出显著减慢。由此导致的高磷酸化tau、淀粉样β和炎症介质的积聚，驱动持续的神经炎症和认知衰退。低强度脉冲超声（LIPUS）在 TBI 小鼠中的神经保护作用已被先前证明，但其对脑淋巴引流的影响尚不清楚。方法：本研究采用受控皮质撞击（CCI）小鼠模型结合连续 LIPUS 刺激，探讨其对 mLV 功能的治疗潜力。结果：LIPUS 恢复了 TBI 小鼠的神经功能，改善了运动协调性和空间/识别记忆，同时减轻了 tau 病理、Aβ 负荷和星形胶质细胞反应。机制上，LIPUS 激活了脑膜淋巴内皮细胞（LECs）上的 Piezo1，触发下游信号级联，促进 LEC 在体外的增殖和迁移，并在体内恢复淋巴覆盖和引流功能。为识别该过程的关键介质，我们检查了该通路的下游组分，发现血管内皮生长因子 C（VEGFC）是关键下游效应物：VEGFC 过表达可恢复脑膜淋巴管和 CSF 引流。结论：这些结果确立了 LIPUS 作为一种非侵入性治疗策略，能够功能性恢复 TBI 后的脑淋巴引流，为与蛋白病相关的神经疾病提供了一种有前景的临床前治疗策略，值得进一步优化以实现临床转化。
